newsitem.title: UK: British MBO boom running out of steam - KPMG.
newsitem.headline: British MBO boom running out of steam - KPMG.

text.p: The boom over the last two years in management buy-outs (MBOs) in Britain looks to be running out of steam, a survey of the market by KPMG Corporate Finance showed on Thursday. The survey showed a marked fall in completions of MBOs in the third quarter, where deals finalised fell to 820 million stg -- the lowest quarterly figure since the beginning of 1995. The third quarter figures compared with 1.08 billion stg seen in the second three months of this year and 890 million in the third quarter of last year.

"We are definitely seeing a lull in the MBO market," said Mike Stevens, head of MBO services at KPMG. "...After the huge prices paid in recent months by some MBO financiers, sellers are expecting too much." Stevens said venture capitalists are right to be cautious as prices asked are usually high and, in some cases, "way over the top."
KPMG said it expects the total value of MBO deals this year to fall well below the total of 6.7 billion stg seen in 1995.
